In the module system, if a public definition is tagged with inline but not expose, is it inlined when imported and used in another file?

My initial thought was no, and I saw that macro_inline would indeed result in an error without expose. But then always_inline doesn't seem to cause an error without expose, so I wasn't sure any more.
expose is for exposing the value, i.e. docs#Lean.Expr of a definition. However, inline only needs the IR, i.e. the docs#Lean.Compiler.LCNF.Decl, which is also available without expose.
So is macro_inline done before IR is generated, and hence the expose requirement?
Yes, macro_inline, as opposed to inline, is done before producing IR. It basically just unfolds every macro_inline function before converting to IR.
